title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 1
paragraphs: When the news of the battle at Marathon reached Darius son of Hystaspes, the king — who had already been greatly angered at the Athenians on account of the attack on Sardis — became more furious still, and more eager than ever to march against Greece. He at once sent messengers round to the various cities and ordered them to prepare a force, assigning to each people a quota far greater than before, and not only warships but also cavalry, supplies, and transport vessels. When these orders went out, all Asia was in motion for three years as the best men were being enlisted for the expedition against Greece and were making ready. In the fourth year, however, the Egyptians, whom Cambyses had reduced to subjection, revolted from the Persians, and then Darius was more eager still to march against both peoples.
